core: Working definition: primates are the order of mammals that includes prosimians, monkeys, apes, and humans

Hallmark primate traits: grasping hands (opposable thumbs, five digits, flat nails, tactile pads), forward-facing eyes (binocular vision, depth perception, postorbital bars, reduced smell), relatively large brains
The three groups: prosimians, monkeys, apes — one line and one original example each
The ape connection: humans are apes (Hominoidea), sharing ancestry with today's great apes rather than descending from them
Primate behavior: sociality, tool use, communication — one line each, factual
Honest note: primate studies illuminate humans without reducing us to them
Honest framing: living primates are our cousins, not our ancestors

claims.claim: Primates are an order of mammals that includes prosimians, monkeys, apes, and humans; humans are part of the biological group known as primates.

Primate hands and feet are built for grasping: opposable thumbs (and opposable big toes in nonhuman primates), five digits, flat nails instead of curved claws, and pads at the fingertips made of fat and nerve deposits.
Primates rely on vision more than smell: eyes face forward, giving binocular vision and depth perception; postorbital bars (bony rings) completely surround the eyes; the snout is relatively small.
Primates have relatively large brains for their body size compared with most other mammals, along with a relatively slow reproductive rate.
Scientists divide the order Primates into two suborders: Strepsirrhini (prosimians: lemurs, lorises, and galagos) and Haplorrhini (tarsiers, New World monkeys, Old World monkeys, apes, and humans).
New World monkeys (Platyrrhini) have nostrils that open to the sides and many have prehensile tails; Old World monkeys (Cercopithecoidea) have downward-facing nostrils and lack prehensile tails.
Apes form the superfamily Hominoidea — gibbons, orangutans, gorillas, chimpanzees, bonobos, and humans — distinguished among living primates by having no tail and being largely terrestrial.
Humans are apes: physical and genetic similarities show that Homo sapiens has a very close relationship to the apes, and the human species sits within Hominoidea.

Humans are not descended from chimpanzees, monkeys, or any other living primate; humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor dating to between 8 and 6 million years ago, and apes and monkeys share a more distant relative from about 25 million years ago.
Most nonhuman primates live in social groups, and they are very vocal and communicative with members of their social group; some nonhuman primates use tools, and some can communicate using symbols.

Primate behavior varies with environment: chimpanzees at Gombe hunt red colobus monkeys with their hands, while chimpanzees at Fongoli adapt sticks into spears to hunt galagos; older chimpanzees teach the young to termite-fish.

Comparative studies of humans and nonhuman primates help anthropologists identify what makes humans human; the Smithsonian describes humans as an unusual species of primate, distinct in traits such as complex symbolic expression and elaborate cultural diversity.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Where do tarsiers belong in primate classification?
positions: Tarsiers share features with both prosimians and anthropoids and were historically grouped with prosimians.
Tarsiers are now classified within Haplorrhini (with monkeys, apes, and humans).
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson follows the current classification (tarsiers within Haplorrhini) and presents the three-group scheme (prosimians, monkeys, apes) as a teaching simplification, with a one-line note that tarsiers are a classification puzzle.

positions: Arboreal theory: traits arose as adaptations to life in the trees.
Visual predation hypothesis (Cartmill): forward-facing eyes and grasping hands aided hunting small prey.
Angiosperm theory: traits co-evolved with flowering plants and fine visual/tactile feeding.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson names the traits as facts and mentions that origin hypotheses exist, without endorsing any single theory; depth on trait origins belongs to the biology subject.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Is the label 'primitive' appropriate for prosimians?
positions: OpenStax describes strepsirrhines as 'primitive' primates that evolved much earlier.
The word can be misread as 'inferior'; every living primate has been evolving for the same length of time.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson avoids the loaded word and describes prosimians as the earliest-evolving group, keeping the factual content while dropping the value-laden label.
